car-stable-angina.title: Stable angina
car-stable-angina.blurb: Exertional chest pressure relieved by rest, confirmed with exercise stress testing.
car-stable-angina.summary: Stable angina presents with exertional chest pressure relieved by rest, typically with reproducible substernal discomfort brought on by climbing stairs. Exercise stress testing confirms it, and antianginal therapy with a beta blocker is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names stable angina is exertional chest pressure relieved by rest; the process behind it is fixed atherosclerotic narrowing of an epicardial coronary artery. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that symptoms are predictable, provoked by exertion, and resolve within minutes of rest or nitroglycerin.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: At the centre of the problem is fixed atherosclerotic narrowing of an epicardial coronary artery. Once that is established, the downstream findings follow in a predictable order, which is what makes the presentation recognisable at the bedside.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes antianginal therapy with a beta blocker the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: The history classically centres on exertional chest pressure relieved by rest; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

Partial or atypical presentations are common enough that the absence of one expected feature should not close the question. A history of exertional chest pressure relieved by rest in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

Findings are easier to elicit once the process is established, so an unrevealing first examination deserves repeating.

car-deep-venous-thrombosis.blurb: Three days of unilateral calf swelling and aching; first step, therapeutic anticoagulation.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names deep venous thrombosis is three days of unilateral calf swelling and aching; the process behind it is venous stasis and hypercoagulability activating the clotting cascade. Sections below follow one conventional sequence — mechanism, presentation, confirmation, management — and each can be read on its own.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that pre-test probability scoring determines whether imaging or D-dimer testing comes first.

paras: At the centre of the problem is venous stasis and hypercoagulability activating the clotting cascade. Once that is established, the downstream findings follow in a predictable order, which is what makes the presentation recognisable at the bedside.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes therapeutic anticoagulation the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: The history classically centres on three days of unilateral calf swelling and aching; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

Findings are easier to elicit once the process is established, so an unrevealing first examination deserves repeating.

The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Prevalence estimates depend heavily on the setting in which they were gathered; referral series and community series describe different populations. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that claudication distance is the functional vital sign to follow over time.

car-mitral-regurgitation.title: Mitral regurgitation
car-mitral-regurgitation.blurb: Slowly progressive dyspnea with fatigue on exertion, confirmed with transthoracic echocardiography.
car-mitral-regurgitation.summary: Mitral regurgitation presents with slowly progressive dyspnea with fatigue on exertion, typically with a holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. Transthoracic echocardiography confirms it, and serial imaging with surgical referral once severity criteria are met is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names mitral regurgitation is slowly progressive dyspnea with fatigue on exertion; the process behind it is incomplete leaflet coaptation permitting systolic backflow into the atrium. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Prevalence estimates depend heavily on the setting in which they were gathered; referral series and community series describe different populations. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that the window for repair is defined by ventricular size and function, not symptoms alone.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe slowly progressive dyspnea with fatigue on exertion, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.
